analysis:
Examined all supplied ProviderLoop.swift BASE excerpts (1–1207) and the complete bounded patch. HEAD 724–735 adds selected-model recovery state, an internal load override, and saved/last-switch enabled-model selections; HEAD 897 initializes the saved selection from configuration. These declarations do not themselves change admission, authorization, encryption, cache isolation, model verification, or billing, so no concrete security regression is established here. Existing process-key generation, attestation signer construction, model eligibility filtering, slot limits, memory budgeting, and slot artifact/cache identities provide relevant surrounding contracts, not proof of the new recovery behavior.
Integration must inspect ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery and its wiring to load, policy-refresh, switch, cancellation, and shutdown paths: ensure recovery respects committed selection and retirement tombstones, uses verified artifacts and memory gates, does not defeat add-on holds or serving drains, and does not revive obsolete work after a switch. Relevant indexed threats include T-012/T-027 (weights), T-010/T-029 (cancellation/residency), T-053 (authorization lifecycle), and T-059/T-060 (hold availability); T-041's supplied cache contract must remain intact during recovered slot construction. Recovery execution and callers are absent from this batch, leaving those material interactions unresolved rather than establishing missing controls.
